items.headline: Chrome zero-day is being exploited
items.summary: Attackers are already exploiting a new bug in Chrome. Visiting one bad web page is enough to run their code on your computer. Google has released a fix, and defenders push the update and check that browsers restarted. This is a test story for the fixture.
items.you: You run Chrome, so this one is yours.

items.headline: One Outlook email can leak your Windows login hash
items.summary: A crafted email makes Outlook connect to an attacker's server and send your Windows login hash, with no click. A hash is a scrambled form of your password that can be cracked or reused. Defenders block outbound SMB and patch Outlook. This is a test story for the fixture.
items.you: SOC view: this is forced authentication, a technique on your path.
items.attack_note: Forced Authentication: the email makes Outlook log in to the attacker's server.

items.headline: Check Point firewall bug exploited at about 24 customers
items.summary: Attackers used a bug in Check Point firewalls to turn a limited login into full control (root) at about 24 customers. Check Point has a fix; defenders patch and review firewall admin logins. This is a test story for the fixture.
items.you: Path: privilege escalation, a limited login became root.
items.attack_note: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation: a limited login becomes root on the firewall.
items.actor: UNC5221: China-linked hackers who target network edge devices.

glossary.meaning: A scrambled, fixed-length form of a password that can be cracked or reused.
The all-powerful admin account on Linux and similar systems.

til.text: Forced authentication tricks a machine into logging in to a server the attacker runs. The login leaks a password hash that can be cracked or relayed. Defenders block outbound SMB and watch for logins to unknown servers.

questions.text: An email made Outlook send your password hash to an attacker's server, with no click. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Forced Authentication: the victim's machine is tricked into authenticating to an attacker's server, leaking a hash.

options: A scrambled form of a password
questions.explanation: A hash is a one-way scrambled form of a password.
